analysis.title: US Equities Color: Risk-Off (5 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities sold off sharply on 5 Nov. S&P closed -4.36% at 7,353 and NDX -6.36% at 26,629. R2K fell 4.46% to 2,729 and the Dow fell 3.44% to 51,523. The market-on-close imbalance was $1.8bn to buy.

Semiconductors and AI-adjacent names led the decline. The desk says the market is recalibrating datacenter gigawatt (GW) build forecasts and the execution path after this week's Election newsflow. Moves were most visible in datacenter construction (E&C) stocks, IPP/Power, Neoclouds and Semiconductors.

SOX multiples have compressed by about 50% from the June/July highs. The desk sees little investor consensus on 2028+ datacenter builds and capex GWs. The debate likely shifts to whether downside risks to GW/capex outlooks have been overpriced.

Desk activity was split. Inbound calls were a 10/10 but overall activity was a 5 out of 10, much quieter than the prior day, which was one of the desk's busiest of the year. The desk attributes price action to top-down macro pressure, with very large notionals traded across the ETF complex.

Asset managers finished net sellers, driven by steady supply in Semis/AI. There was no offsetting bid for Hyperscalers or Defensive Tech, which had supported the index the day before. Hedge fund flows were roughly balanced while they actively toggled short books.

Systematic positioning added pressure. Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). The desk expects incremental US supply in tomorrow's estimates, with the 2.5 standard deviation estimate from the morning at -$7.48bn in S&P for sale over the next week.

Volatility spiked. VIX rose 67.19% to 27.77 and Nasdaq's VIX had its biggest one-day move since Covid. VVIX rose nearly 45 points, the second-largest one-day rise ever behind Volmageddon. VIX vol had its second-largest one-day move higher ever.

Derivatives flow was dominated by hedge monetization early in the session in S&P, Nasdaq and VIX products. NDX and SPX fixed-strike vols were bid aggressively, most in the front end, and skew steepened sharply. Hedges were unwound and restructured, including a client buy of SPY 27Nov 700/730 put spreads, and VIX calls and call spreads were unwound as VIX spiked above 26.
The desk's Vol Panic Index reached 9.3 out of 10 intraday. The index combines 1m S&P implied vol, VIX vol, S&P 1m skew and S&P term structure slope.
Cross-asset moves: WTI +2.80% to $90.58, US 10YR -5bps to 4.83%, gold +0.57% to $4,084, DXY +1bp to 101.58 and Bitcoin -5.47% to $75,870.

Several records were set. NDX had its worst day since March 9, 2020. S&P had its worst day since 4/4/25. SOX fell 12%, its worst day since 2020. High Beta Momentum fell 6.2% and is 51% off its June highs, the worst drawdown in over 10 years. ETFs were 32% of tape volume, the largest share since June.
